text.p: The Royal Dutch/Shell group said on Thursday it was planning a major move into world electricity markets over the next five years.

"We are very dedicated to developing it (electricity) further and I could well see it as a global business," Royal Dutch chairman and head of the group's committee of manging directors Cor Herkstroeter told reporters.
"In the next five years, we will either have made substantial progress or decide not to go ahead with it," he said.
Herkstroeter added he saw strong growth in electricity markets particularly in Asia and more specifically in countries such as China.
"The electricity markets will grow a lot in coming years," he said.
Investments to build up a strong position could be substantial in due course, but Herkstroeter said Shell, one of the world's biggest oil companies, would move cautiously.
He did not rule out acquisitions but said none were planned at the moment. "First of all we need a satisfactory base to start from and take it from there," he said.
To get more acquainted with electricity markets worldwide, Shell was bringing in experts from outside the company and might decide to form a different division to boost its presence.

Shell, which has already decided to start modest electricity operations in the Philippines and Namibia, said it would focus on power generation, but did not rule out getting involved in in electricity distribution too.
Herkstroeter said Anglo-Dutch Shell was not targeting specific areas in the world.
Speaking more generally on Shell's electricity plans, he said: "You will hear more about it in due course."
